name: Acute Encephalopathy with Biphasic Seizures and Late Reduced Diffusion
aliases: Acute Encephalopathy with Biphasic Seizures and Delayed Reduced Diffusion

ethnicAssociations: East Asian populations (notably Japanese and Korean)

criteria.description: Presence of biphasic seizures with initial prolonged febrile seizure followed by secondary cluster seizures after a lucid interval
MRI showing late reduced diffusion in subcortical white matter typically appearing 3-9 days after initial seizure
Preceding febrile illness or infection within 1 week prior to onset
Prolonged altered level of consciousness lasting more than 24 hours

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Biphasic seizures plus late reduced diffusion on MRI with altered consciousness
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and radiological; exclusion of other causes of encephalopathy is essential

common.symptomName: Hypointensity of cerebral white matter on MRI
Abnormal metabolic brain imaging by MRS

occasional.symptomName: Status epilepticus without prominent motor symptoms

laboratory: Mild elevation of inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR)
Normal or mildly elevated liver enzymes
imaging: MRI brain showing late reduced diffusion in subcortical white matter (typically days 3-9)
Absence of early diffusion abnormalities in initial phase
Possible cerebral edema in severe cases
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing diffuse slowing and epileptiform discharges during acute phase

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of late reduced diffusion on MRI
MRI shows multifocal demyelinating lesions rather than subcortical reduced diffusion
Often follows viral infection or vaccination
Different MRI patterns including stroke-like lesions

redFlags: Development of secondary cluster seizures after initial seizure
Late appearance of reduced diffusion on MRI indicating ongoing brain injury
references: Takanashi J. Acute encephalopathy with biphasic seizures and late reduced diffusion (AESD): clinical features and prognosis. Brain Dev. 2012.
Yamamoto Y, et al. MRI findings and clinical features of AESD in children. Neurology. 2015.
Orphanet: Acute encephalopathy with biphasic seizures and late reduced diffusion (ORPHA:363549)
